headline: Hormuz tensions resurface and PSX gives back part of its two-day rally, while Lotte Chemical's blowout Q2 results and confirmed dividend steal the day's spotlight.
summary: PSX opened lower Friday (-0.31%) as renewed US-Iran tension over the Strait of Hormuz snapped back after Thursday's dialogue-hope rally, with banks, E&P and OMCs leading declines. Brent near $84.6 and a still-maxed conflict-stress reading keep the desk's geo-risk gauge at 'moderate,' even as domestic anchors stay solid — CPI eased to 11.1%, SBP holds rates, reserves near $18.5bn. The standout story is Lotte Chemical: Q2 EPS jumped to Rs1.87 with a confirmed Rs1.50/share dividend, driving the day's heaviest volume. The desk leans cautious near-term, watching whether Hormuz de-escalates again before chasing Thursday's bounce.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: Rate-hold backdrop plus some of the cheapest, best-covered dividends on the board (HBL 7.9% yield/48% payout, MCB 9.1%/74%, NBP 17.1%/22%) — but MCB, MEBL, NBP and UBL all opened red this morning on the Hormuz headline, so it reads as a pullback to watch, not a clean signal yet.

sectors.name: E&P
sectors.why: Direct beneficiary of Brent holding near $84-85 and the macro desk's own sector tilt favours it, but OGDC, PPL and MARI are whipsawing on every Hormuz headline (PPL is down almost 6% over five sessions and trading below its 50-day average) — a volatile hold, not a clean trend.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Domestic-demand defensive with low direct oil-import exposure per the macro desk's own tilt; ENGROH screens outright cheap (P/E 5.3, 10% net margin) and FFC pays a well-covered 6.7% yield, both among Thursday's biggest rebound contributors.

sectors.name: OMCs & refineries
sectors.why: Weekly-repriced fuel costs and circular-debt risk are exactly what today's petroleum price review (2026-07-17, Brent still near $84-85) threatens to aggravate — PSO's net margin is just 1.4%, leaving little cushion for another hike.

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: FY26 car sales jumped 39% and two names (HCAR, GAL) are showing live technical triggers today, but the macro desk flags autos to avoid on imported-input cost exposure, and both carry thin-margin or 'caution' fundamental flags underneath the momentum.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Energy-cost-sensitive like autos, but LUCK, DGKC, MLCF and FCCL are all rated only 'mixed' fundamentally with no active technical trigger today — no strong read either way right now.

watchlist.angle: Williams %R mid cross is triggering now (63% hit rate over 27 trades, +1.1% net/trade, still positive out-of-sample) on a name the desk already reads as cheap — P/E 5.3, healthy 10% net margin, ultra-low beta (0.05). It was among the biggest point-contributors to Thursday's rebound and rose 3.4% Wednesday.
watchlist.risk: It's a low-confidence signal (modest sample, modest edge) on a stock that's normally low-volatility — a fresh Hormuz flare that hits the broad index hard would likely erase the edge fast.

watchlist.angle: 2-ATR stretch below the 20-day average is triggering (69% hit rate over 13 trades, +1.2% net/trade) after a sharp one-day snapback. Fundamentals back it up: 43% net margin and a moderate, covered 4.6% dividend.
watchlist.risk: Small-cap (Rs24.7bn market cap) with a thin backtest sample for this exact signal — light-volume names like this can gap through a 7-session mean-reversion hold quickly if the bounce stalls.

watchlist.angle: Trend + momentum combo is triggering (56% hit rate, 39 trades) riding Pakistan's 39% FY26 car-sales jump; fundamentals show a cheap 4.96x P/E and improving forward earnings with 12-13% net margins.
watchlist.risk: It's a low-confidence signal in a small, high-beta name (0.92) inside a sector the macro desk currently flags to avoid on import-cost exposure — today's fuel-price review could undercut the demand story fast.

watchlist.angle: Golden cross (SMA50>SMA200) is the desk's highest-confidence trigger today — 60% hit rate over 10 trades, +3.1% net/trade, still profitable out-of-sample — landing right into the FY26 car-sales strength (+39% YoY).
watchlist.risk: Fundamentals flag outright caution: net margin is just 2.6%, and a thin-margin auto name is exactly what a weaker rupee or a fresh fuel hike squeezes first — autos are explicitly on the macro desk's avoid list.

watchlist.angle: The day's real story: Q2CY26 EPS jumped to Rs1.87 (from Rs0.97 in Q1) on higher sales and profit, with a confirmed Rs1.50/share cash dividend (book closure 2026-07-27, buy-by 2026-07-24) and the heaviest trading volume on the board this week — news-sentinel flagged it impact-4.
watchlist.risk: Fundamentals still rate 'caution' — net margin is thin at 5.5% and the payout ratio is a stretched 161% of earnings, so the dividend's sustainability is a real question; no proven technical strategy is currently triggering here, so this is a catalyst play, not a backtested setup.

catalysts.event: Weekly petroleum price review — Brent still near $84-85 makes a further hike or flat roll more likely than a cut
LOTCHEM ex-dividend buy-by date ahead of book closure
SBP MPC — first monetary policy decision of FY27
LOTCHEM book closure begins (dividend Rs1.50/share, confirmed)

risks: The Strait of Hormuz conflict is not confirmed de-escalating — fresh US strikes and an active naval blockade were still reported this week, and today's tape shows the market pricing that back in after two days of assuming it was contained.
Today's petroleum price review lands with Brent still elevated near $84-85; a further pump-price hike would add to inflation and squeeze OMC margins that are already thin.

Wednesday-Thursday's rally (+1.02%, +1.62%) ran ahead of the wire tape, which was still showing the conflict intensifying rather than cooling — a genuine but fragile divergence that could unwind if the geo-risk score stays pinned at maximum on the conflict factor.
disclaimer: Research, not advice. The desk generates signals; it does not place orders. Losses are expected.
